correctness.rationale: The unique maximal-length factor yields full zero/one counts Z,O. Single-symbol spectra yield longest runs M_0,M_1. Cases with at most three runs are reconstructed by those totals. For four vs five runs, the existence of factors with all zeros but fewer than all ones and conversely distinguishes the cases and the external color. At four runs the min zero count at O and first j with U(j)=Z give the central zero length and first one length. At five runs L(O) gives the central zero run, U(max(b,d)) gives the larger outer zero run, while U(min(b,d)) resolves the pairing with the shorter one-run unless the pairing is immaterial up to reversal. The six-run collision family has each asserted spectrum row for j=0,1,2,3; the short words below seven cannot admit a nonreversal collision by the five-run proof or alternation at length six. Independently enumerated all <=5-run binary words of lengths 1–11 (2,046 examined) and complete Parikh sets, and directly checked the six-run collision for 2<=t<=19. Finite evidence corroborates, not replaces, the full run reconstruction argument.

value.rationale: Yes/no jumbled indexing loses factor order and multiplicity; identifying exactly how many symbol runs remain invertible is a meaningful sharp reconstruction invariant. The theorem proves full reconstruction up to the inherent reversal symmetry on a maximal low-complexity class and supplies an explicit infinite counterexample family at the first forbidden run count and minimal length.

final_claim: For any nonempty binary words u,v each having at most five runs, equality of the sets of contiguous-factor Parikh vectors implies v=u or reversal(u). For t>=2, u_t=0101 0^t 1 and v_t=01 0^t 101 are different nonreversals with six runs, identical Parikh support; seven is the smallest length at which any collision exists.
limitations: Alphabet labels fixed; reversal unavoidable; Parikh vectors are sets without multiplicities.
